mainTopic: Testing תכלת, buying ציצית, and who is obligated in ציצית
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's discussion of how to test whether blue wool was dyed with real תכלת. It brings two tests: soaking the wool overnight, and baking it in hard barley dough. The ברייתא's claim that תכלת 'has no test' is explained as meaning only that you cannot tell whether the wool was dyed as a trial dip. When תכלת from מר ממשכי failed one test and passed the other, רב אחאי showed that the two tests work together in order, and a message from ארץ ישראל confirmed this. The גמרא then discusses buying a טלית with ציצית from the market, and why a Jew may not sell one to a non-Jew. It explains רב יהודה's practice of putting ציצית on his wife's garment and making a ברכה every morning. Finally, it brings a ברייתא on who is obligated in ציצית. It explains why כהנים are included, and shows רבי שמעון's source for exempting women: a night garment is exempt, so ציצית is time-bound. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to ask how the רבנן read that פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the soaking test for real תכלת
steps.stepSummary: The soaking test of רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה ends: soak the wool overnight. If the color fades, it is פסולה; if not, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The urine must be forty days old. He soaks the wool in this mixture from evening until morning. If its color fades, it is unfit. If its color does not fade, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a test that started on the previous line. It explains how to check whether blue wool was dyed with real תכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real תכלת holds its color even after a harsh overnight soak. Fake dye fades. The fact that such a test exists challenges the ברייתא, which said תכלת cannot be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: its appearance/color faded or came apart

phrases.english: forty days old,
and he soaks it in them
phrases.notes: "It" is the blue wool. "Them" is the mixture of ingredients.

phrases.english: from evening until morning.
If its color faded, it is unfit;
if its color did not fade, it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, וְתָרֵי לַהּ בְּגַוַּויְיהוּ מֵאוּרְתָּא וְעַד לְצַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the test begun before this section, as part of the challenge to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool that keeps its color after an overnight soak is real תכלת and כשרה. Wool that fades is פסולה.

steps.title: A second test: baking the wool in barley dough
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא, in the name of רב עוירא, gives another test: bake the wool inside hard barley dough. If the color gets better, it is כשרה; if it gets worse, it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said before רבא in the name of רב עוירא: Bring hard leavened barley dough and bake the wool inside it. If the color changes for the better, it is fit. If it changes for the worse, it is unfit. Your memory sign is: change shows falsehood, change shows truth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way to test תכלת. This adds more pressure on the ברייתא that said there is no test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This test works the opposite way from the first. Here the color is expected to change: real תכלת gets stronger, and fake dye gets weaker. With two separate tests on record, the claim that תכלת 'has no test' looks even harder to defend.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two tests. In the soaking test, real תכלת should NOT change at all. In the baking test, real תכלת SHOULD change, by getting better.

phrases.english: And Rav Adda, before Rava,
in the name of Rav Avira, said:
One brings hard leavened barley dough
and bakes it inside it.
phrases.notes: He bakes the wool inside the dough.

phrases.english: If it changed for the better, it is fit;
if for the worse, it is unfit.
And your memory sign is:
change of falsehood, change of truth.
phrases.notes: Both kinds of wool change. The fake one changes for the worse, and the real one changes for the better.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַדָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוִּירָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second test alongside the first, strengthening the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that תכלת has no test.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two working tests for real תכלת exist, so how can the ברייתא say there is no test?

steps.title: What 'no test' really means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא only means you cannot tell whether wool was dyed as a trial dip (טעימה).
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the ברייתא mean when it says, 'it has no test'? It means there is no test regarding a trial dip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what the ברייתא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tests can show whether the dye is real תכלת. They cannot show whether the wool was dyed for the מצוה or only as a trial dip to check the dye, which makes it פסולה. So the ברייתא and the tests do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'tasting': a trial dip of wool to test the dye

steps.whatToRemember: The tests can show whether the dye is real. No test can show whether it was dyed for the מצוה rather than as a trial dip.

phrases.english: What does it mean when it says, "it has no test"?
Regarding a trial dip.
phrases.notes: A trial dip means dipping wool just to check the dye. Wool dyed that way is not valid for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised by the two tests.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'no test' meant you cannot tell real תכלת from fake.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No test' means you cannot tell whether the wool was dyed as a trial dip.

steps.title: The תכלת from משכי fails one test and passes the other
steps.stepSummary: מר ממשכי brought תכלת in the days of רב אחאי. It failed the soaking test but passed the baking test.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר from משכי brought תכלת in the years of רב אחאי. They tested it by the method of רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה, and its color faded. Then they tested it by the method of רב אדא, and it changed for the better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where the two tests gave opposite results. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first test the wool is פסולה, but by the second it is כשרה. That raises a real practical problem: what do you do when the two tests disagree?

keyTerms.meaning: תכלת: the special blue dye or blue wool

steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows the two tests can conflict. The גמרא must now work out how to rule in such a case.

phrases.english: Mar from Mashkhei brought sky-blue wool
in the years of Rav Achai.

phrases.aramaic: בַּדְקוּהָ בִּדְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: They tested it by the method of Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the overnight soaking test from step 1.

phrases.english: and its color faded;
by the method of Rav Adda,
phrases.notes: This is the barley-dough baking test from step 2.

phrases.english: and it changed for the better.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר מִמִּשְׁכִּי אַיְיתִי תְּכֵלְתָּא בִּשְׁנֵי רַב אַחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies both tests to a real case and shows they conflict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this real case, the two tests gave opposite results. Steps 5 and 6 explain how to rule.

steps.title: רב אחאי objects to rejecting the wool
steps.stepSummary: The scholars wanted to reject the wool for failing the soaking test. רב אחאי objects: then it is neither תכלת nor קלא אילן, which is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to declare it unfit. רב אחאי said to them: But then this is not תכלת, and it is not indigo either?!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars lean toward rejecting מר ממשכי's wool, and רב אחאי challenges that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each test stands on its own, the wool failed one test, so it is not תכלת. But it passed the other test, so it is not fake indigo either. Every dyed wool must be one or the other, so treating the tests separately leads to an impossible result.

keyTerms.meaning: real תכלת, the kosher blue dye
indigo, the plant dye that looks like תכלת but is not kosher

phrases.english: They thought to declare it unfit,
Rav Achai said to them:
But then is this not תכלת,
and also not indigo?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the strange result of the story in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to reject the wool because it failed only the soaking test.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Treating the two tests as separate gives an impossible result: wool that is neither תכלת nor קלא אילן.

steps.title: The two tests work together in order
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי concludes that the two tests go together: soak first; if the color stays, it is kosher; if it fades, bake it, and the result of the baking decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the two teachings were said together. When we test it the way of רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה: if its color did not fade, it is kosher. If its color faded, we test it the way of רב אדא with hard barley dough: if it changed for the better, it is kosher; if for the worse, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי solves the problem by saying the two tests are steps of one process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soaking test can only approve wool, not reject it. If the color fades, we do not reject it yet; we move on to the baking test, which gives the final answer. So מר ממשכי's wool, which faded but then passed the baking test, is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: the teachings were said together, as one combined process

steps.whatToRemember: The order is: soak first. Color stays: kosher. Color fades: bake it. Gets better: kosher. Gets worse: unfit.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that the teachings were said together.
Where we tested it
by the method of Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah,
if its color did not fade, it is kosher;
if its color faded,
we test it by the method of Rav Adda,
with hard leavened barley dough:
if it changed for the better, it is kosher;
for the worse, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁמוּעָתָא אַהֲדָדֵי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two separate teachings into one ordered process.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each test is a full test by itself, so failing either one makes the wool unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The soaking test can only approve wool. If the color fades, the baking test decides.

steps.title: A message from ארץ ישראל confirms it
steps.stepSummary: A message from ארץ ישראל confirms that the two teachings were said together.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: the teachings were said together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for רב אחאי's idea from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחאי worked this out by logic. Now a tradition from ארץ ישראל says the same thing, so his reading is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: they sent from there, meaning a message from ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: The teachings were said together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחאי's claim that the two tests work together.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A message from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי מני buys תכלת carefully
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני was careful to buy תכלת following the strict rules of the ברייתא. An old man praised him, saying earlier generations did the same and did well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני was careful and bought according to the strict rules of the ברייתא. A certain old man said to him: This is what those before you did, and their business did well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about someone who was very careful when buying תכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no test to tell if wool was dyed as a trial dip (Step 3), the safe way is to buy only from an expert. רבי מני did this, and the old man told him this careful practice brings success.

keyTerms.meaning: the strict rules of the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani was careful and bought
according to the strict rules of the ברייתא,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא from Step 3: wool dyed as a trial dip is not kosher, so buy only from an expert.

phrases.english: A certain old man said to him:
This is what those who came before you did,
and their business did well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מָנִי דָּיֵיק וְזָבֵין כְּחוּמְרֵי מַתְנְיָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from testing תכלת to the practical way of buying it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is praiseworthy to buy תכלת only in the strict way, from an expert.

steps.title: Buying a טלית with ציצית in the market
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a טלית with ציצית bought from a Jew keeps its kosher status. From a non-Jew, if he is a merchant it is kosher; if he is a regular person, it is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who buys a טלית with ציצית from the market: from a Jew, it keeps its presumed status. From a non-Jew: from a merchant, it is kosher; from a regular person, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about when we can trust the ציצית on a טלית bought in the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew is trusted, so the טלית keeps its kosher status. A non-Jewish merchant cares about his name, so he would buy from a reliable source. A regular non-Jew may have made the blue strings himself, so they are unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: a garment that already has ציצית on it
in its presumed status, so we assume it is kosher
a regular person, not a professional

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who buys a garment with ציצית from the market,
from a Jew, it keeps its presumed status;
from a non-Jew: from a merchant, it is kosher;
from a regular person, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of buying ציצית and תכלת from trustworthy sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From a Jew it keeps its status; from a non-Jewish merchant it is kosher; from a regular non-Jew it is unfit.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two non-Jews: a merchant (תגר) is trusted, but a regular person (הדיוט) is not.

steps.title: Do not sell a garment with ציצית to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a rule: a Jew may not sell a טלית with ציצית to a non-Jew until he removes the ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the חכמים said that a person may not sell a cloak with ציצית to a non-Jew until he unties its ציצית, we still trust a non-Jewish merchant.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its teaching from the last step. It says a Jew may not sell a garment with ציצית to a non-Jew without first taking the ציצית off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we learned that a טלית bought from a non-Jewish merchant is kosher. This line explains why that is surprising: Jews are not supposed to sell such garments to non-Jews. Even so, we assume the merchant got it from a Jew who did not follow this rule, so the ציצית are still kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment that already has ציצית tied on it

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not cancel step 9. The rule here is about a Jew selling to a non-Jew. Step 9 is about a Jew buying from a non-Jewish merchant. Buying from the merchant is still kosher.

phrases.english: And even though they said:
A person is not permitted to sell
a cloak with ritual fringes to a non-Jew
until he unties its fringes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 9 by adding a related rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may not sell a טלית with ציצית to a non-Jew unless he first removes the ציצית.

steps.title: Why is it forbidden to sell it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it is forbidden to sell a garment with ציצית to a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule it just learned. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what danger or problem the rule is guarding against.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a Jew may not sell a garment with ציצית to a non-Jew.

steps.title: Two reasons: shame, or danger on the road
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: in בבל they said it is because of a זונה. רב יהודה said a Jew might travel with him and be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained it is because of a זונה: the non-Jew may visit a זונה while looking like a Jew. רב יהודה said: a Jew might join him on the road, thinking he is Jewish, and the non-Jew might kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different reasons for the rule. Both reasons come from the same worry: people will think the non-Jew is a Jew because of his ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about shame: people would think a Jew is doing something immoral. The second reason is about physical danger: a Jew might trust him as a fellow Jew and be harmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps he will go along with him

steps.whatToRemember: The ציצית make the non-Jew look Jewish. This can bring shame on Jews (a זונה) or put a Jew in danger (travelling with him).

phrases.english: Here they explained
phrases.notes: "Here" means in בבל, where the גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: because of a prostitute.
phrases.notes: The non-Jew might visit a זונה, and people would think a Jew was doing it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Perhaps a Jew will join him on the road
and he will kill him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either because of shame (he might visit a זונה looking Jewish) or because of danger (a Jew might travel with him and be killed).

steps.title: רב יהודה put תכלת on his wife's garment
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה attached תכלת to his wife's garment, and every morning he made the ברכה "להתעטף בציצית".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה would attach תכלת to the garment of his wife, and every morning he would make the ברכה: "to wrap ourselves in ציצית".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a story about what רב יהודה did. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facts are given here. First, he put ציצית on his wife's garment, which shows women are obligated. Second, he made a new ברכה every morning. The גמרא will ask how both fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: "To wrap ourselves in ציצית": the ברכה on ציצית

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would attach sky-blue strings
to the garment of the members of his household,
phrases.notes: "His household" here means his wife.

phrases.english: and he would make a blessing every morning:
"To wrap ourselves in ritual fringes."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה רָמֵי תְּכֵילְתָּא לְפַרְזוּמָא דְּאִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about רב יהודה's practice with ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה put ציצית on his wife's garment and made a ברכה on ציצית every morning.

steps.title: If ציצית is not time-bound, why a ברכה every morning?
steps.stepSummary: Since he put ציצית on his wife's garment, he must hold ציצית is a מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא. If so, why did he make a new ברכה every morning?
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that he attached ציצית to his wife's garment, we see he holds it is a מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא. If so, why did he make a ברכה every single morning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב יהודה's two practices seem to contradict each other. It asks how they can fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are only obligated in a מצות עשה that is not tied to time. So putting ציצית on his wife's garment means ציצית applies at night too. But if the מצוה goes on through the night, morning is not a new start, so why a new ברכה each morning?

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה that is not tied to a set time; women are obligated in it

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that a ברכה is wrong. The question is only why there is a NEW ברכה each morning, if the מצוה never stopped during the night.

phrases.english: From the fact that he attaches them, he holds:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הוּא,
phrases.english: it is a positive מצוה that is not time-bound.
So why does he make a blessing
each and every morning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 13 by showing the two practices seem to clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's practice of making a new ברכה on ציצית every morning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Putting ציצית on his wife's garment shows he holds ציצית is not time-bound, so it applies at night too. Then morning is not a new start, and a new ברכה each morning makes no sense.

steps.title: רב יהודה followed רבי: each new wearing gets a new blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה made a new ברכה each morning because he held like רבי, who says you make a ברכה on תפילין every time you put them on.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held like רבי. A ברייתא teaches: every time a person puts on תפילין, he makes a ברכה on them. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. רב יהודה's daily ברכה follows the opinion of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if ציצית is not tied to a time of day, the obligation never stops, so why make a new ברכה every morning? The answer is that, according to רבי, the ברכה is tied to each act of putting the item on, not to the start of a new day. So each new wearing deserves its own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, the boxes worn on the head and arm
He makes a ברכה over them

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a rule about ברכות: according to רבי, a new act of doing the מצוה brings a new ברכה, even several times a day.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi, as it is taught:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Tefillin: every time one puts them on
he makes a blessing on them. These are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties רב יהודה's practice to a known תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One ברכה should cover ציצית for all time, since the obligation never stops.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי, every new putting-on gets its own ברכה.

steps.title: Then he should bless every time he puts it on
steps.stepSummary: If every putting-on needs a ברכה, רב יהודה should have made a ברכה many times a day, not just once in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also make a ברכה every time he puts it on during the day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If every wearing needs a ברכה, why only once a day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי's rule, the ברכה should follow each act of putting the garment on. People take off their cloaks and put them back on during the day. So רב יהודה's single morning ברכה does not seem to fit רבי's rule either.

phrases.english: If so, every time as well!
phrases.notes: He means: each time he took off his cloak and put it back on, he should have made another ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב יהודה followed רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's rule would require a ברכה at every wearing, not only once each morning.

steps.title: רב יהודה never took off his cloak during the day
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה was very modest and kept his cloak on all day, so there was never a second putting-on during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was a modest man, and he did not take off his cloak the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: there was only one putting-on each day, because רב יהודה never removed his cloak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's rule still applies; there simply were no extra wearings to bless. Since the cloak stayed on all day, one ברכה was enough.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was a modest man,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שָׁרֵי לֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא.
phrases.english: and he did not take off his cloak the whole day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He took his cloak on and off, so he should have blessed many times.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never took it off during the day, so only one ברכה was needed.

steps.title: What made the morning different?
steps.stepSummary: If he wore it all day long, why did the morning call for a new ברכה at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is different about the morning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If he never took it off, what new act in the morning called for a ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, a ברכה is tied to a new act of putting the garment on. If the cloak always stayed on, the morning should be no different from any other time. So why bless then?

phrases.english: And what is different about the morning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The morning ברכה, given that he never removed his cloak
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there was no new putting-on, the morning ברכה has no reason.

steps.title: In the morning he switched from night clothes to day clothes
steps.stepSummary: In the morning רב יהודה changed from his night garment into his day garment, which was a real new putting-on.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made the ברכה when he changed from his nighttime garment to his daytime garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the morning was when he put on a different garment, the day garment, so it was a new wearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He kept the day cloak on all day, but at night he wore other clothing. Each morning he really did put on a garment anew, and that new putting-on is what earned the ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה followed רבי: each new putting-on gets a ברכה. Since he changed garments only once a day, in the morning, he made the ברכה only then.

phrases.english: When he changes from a night garment
to a day garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְשַׁנֵּי מִכְּסוּת לַיְלָה לִכְסוּת יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18 and closes the discussion of רב יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing new happened in the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the morning he changed into his day garment, which was a new putting-on.

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in ציצית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists who is obligated in ציצית: כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, גרים, נשים and עבדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Everyone is obligated in ציצית: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, גרים, women and slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who must wear ציצית. This is the first opinion, the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא includes women in the list. That means he does not treat ציצית as a מצוה tied to a time of day, the same view the גמרא linked to רב יהודה, who put ציצית on his wife's garment.

keyTerms.meaning: The fringes on a four-cornered garment

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Everyone is obligated in tzitzit:
priests, Levites and Israelites,
converts, women and slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: who is obligated in ציצית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Jews, including women, converts and slaves, are obligated in ציצית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts women because ציצית is time-bound
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and exempts women, because ציצית is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from all such מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון exempts women, because it is a positive מצוה that depends on time, and women are exempt from every positive מצוה that depends on time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion. רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא about women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that ציצית applies only by day, not at night, which makes it a time-bound מצוה. Since women are exempt from positive time-bound מצוות, they are exempt from ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה caused, meaning limited, by time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. The תנא קמא obligates women in ציצית; only רבי שמעון exempts them, because he treats ציצית as tied to time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts women,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמִּצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָאּ הוּא,
phrases.english: because it is a positive מצוה caused by time,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָאּ נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת.
phrases.english: and from every positive מצוה caused by time, women are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from ציצית because it is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא.

steps.title: Why say כהנים, לוים and ישראלים? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא and asks why it needed to list כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, since if they were exempt, nobody would be obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: Everyone is obligated in ציצית, כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. But that is obvious! If כהנים, לוים and ישראלים were exempt, who would be obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to analyze the ברייתא line by line. It challenges the first part as saying something too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three groups make up the entire Jewish people, so of course they are obligated. A ברייתא does not waste words, so there must be a hidden point in listing them. The answer will come next.

phrases.english: The Master said: Everyone is obligated in tzitzit,
phrases.notes: "The Master" just means the ברייתא we quoted a moment ago.

phrases.english: priests, Levites and Israelites.
That is obvious!
For if priests, Levites and Israelites were exempt,
who would be obligated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּצִיצִית, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins analyzing the wording of the ברייתא from step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The listing of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These groups make up all of the Jewish people. Listing them seems to add nothing, and a ברייתא should not state the obvious.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא had to mention כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to list כהנים, because we might have thought that since כלאים is permitted to them, they are exempt from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to mention כהנים. You might have thought: the תורה puts 'Do not wear שעטנז, wool and linen together' right next to 'Make yourself fringes.' So only someone who may not wear כלאים is obligated in ציצית. כהנים, who are allowed to wear כלאים, should then be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22. It explains the mistaken idea we might have had about כהנים, and this sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים about שעטנז and ציצית sit next to each other, so we might link them. The idea would be that ציצית only applies to people who are forbidden in כלאים. A כהן wears כלאים in his בגדי כהונה, so we might have exempted him from ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (the ברייתא) to say it
You might have thought (a הוה אמינא, a first idea that turns out wrong)
A forbidden mixture of wool and linen
Forbidden mixtures; here, wool and linen together in clothing

phrases.english: Priests: it was necessary for him to mention them,
since it might enter your mind to say:
Since it is written,
'You shall not wear a forbidden mixture,
wool and linen together.
You shall make yourself fringes,'

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּלָא אִישְׁתְּרִי כִּלְאַיִם לְגַבֵּיהּ בִּלְבִישָׁה
phrases.english: whoever is not permitted to wear כלאים
phrases.notes: Because the two פסוקים are right next to each other, we might connect the two מצוות.

phrases.english: is the one who is obligated in ציצית.
These priests,
since כלאים is permitted to them,
phrases.notes: The כהן's belt in the בגדי כהונה is made of wool and linen.

phrases.english: should not be obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22's question about why כהנים needed to be listed, at least for כהנים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the listing is needed to block a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the שעטנז and ציצית פסוקים are side by side, only those forbidden in כלאים are obligated in ציצית, so כהנים are exempt.

steps.title: כהנים are permitted כלאים only during the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that כהנים are obligated, because כלאים is permitted to them only while they do the עבודה, not at other times.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ברייתא teaches us: even though כלאים is permitted to them while they do the עבודה, when they are not doing the עבודה it is not permitted. So they are obligated in ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer and rejects the mistaken idea from step 23. כהנים are like everyone else most of the time, so they are obligated in ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we accept the link between כלאים and ציצית, the כהן's permission is narrow: it only applies during the עבודה. Outside that time he is forbidden in כלאים like anyone else, so he is also obligated in ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the real point of the statement)
Granted that... (admits a point but limits it)
The time of the Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: כהנים are obligated in ציצית, since their permission to wear כלאים applies only during the עבודה.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
granted that it is permitted at the time of the service,
when it is not the time of the service, it is not permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: נְהִי דְּאִישְׁתְּרִי בְּעִידָּן עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הוה אמינא of step 23 and gives the real lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלאים permission is limited to the עבודה, so כהנים are obligated in ציצית.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source for exempting women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's view from the ברייתא and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that רבי שמעון exempts women. What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the second part of the ברייתא (step 21) and asks where רבי שמעון gets his exemption for women. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said women are exempt because ציצית is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. The question is how we know ציצית depends on time at all. The גמרא needs a source showing ציצית is tied to day and not night.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts women.
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of כהנים and turns to רבי שמעון's opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that ציצית is a time-bound מצוה.

steps.title: 'וּרְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ' excludes a night garment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'and you shall see it' that a night garment is exempt from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall see it' excludes a night garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Since ציצית must be seen, a garment worn at night is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If night garments are exempt, then ציצית depends on time: day yes, night no. That makes it a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so רבי שמעון exempts women.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this teaches that ציצית is about the person seeing. The point here is the time: at night the garment is exempt, which makes ציצית time-bound.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'And you shall see it',
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:39

phrases.english: excludes a night garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וראיתם אותו' exempts a night garment, so ציצית is time-bound and women are exempt.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק excludes a blind person's garment instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe 'and you shall see it' excludes the garment of a blind person, who cannot see.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it excludes a night garment? Maybe it only excludes the garment of a blind person?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, a challenge is raised against reading the פסוק as being about night. A blind person also cannot see his ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seeing' could mean two different things. It could be about the time (night, when it is dark) or about the person (someone blind). If it means the person, ציצית would not be time-bound and the source for רבי שמעון falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say... or is it perhaps only...? (raises another possible reading)

phrases.english: Do you say it excludes a night garment,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא פְּרָט לִכְסוּת סוֹמֵא?
phrases.english: or does it only exclude the garment of a blind person?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: פְּרָט לִכְסוּת לַיְלָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא פְּרָט לִכְסוּת סוֹמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'וראיתם אותו' excludes a night garment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blind person also cannot see, so the פסוק could be excluding him instead of night.

steps.title: 'אֲשֶׁר תְּכַסֶּה בָּהּ' includes the blind, so the exclusion must be night
steps.stepSummary: A different פסוק includes a blind person's garment, so 'וראיתם אותו' must be excluding a night garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'with which you cover yourself,' a blind person's garment is already included. So how do I explain 'and you shall see it'? It excludes a night garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own challenge. Another פסוק already includes the blind person, so the exclusion of 'seeing' must be about night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'אשר תכסה בה' teach that any garment a person covers himself with needs ציצית, even a blind person's. So the blind person can't be what 'וראיתם אותו' excludes. That leaves night, which keeps ציצית time-bound and supports רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אשר תכסה בה' includes a blind person's garment, so 'וראיתם אותו' excludes a night garment. This makes ציצית time-bound, which is רבי שמעון's source for exempting women.

phrases.english: When it says, 'with which you cover yourself,'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:12. The extra words include any garment a person wears, even if he cannot see.

phrases.english: the garment of a blind person is already stated as included.
So how do I apply 'and you shall see it'?
It excludes a night garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: אֲשֶׁר תְּכַסֶּה בָּהּ, הֲרֵי כְּסוּת סוֹמֵא אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 and confirms the reading of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another פסוק covers the other option, so the exclusion must refer to night
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וראיתם אותו' might exclude a blind person's garment.
steps.terutzMaskana: A blind person's garment is included by 'אשר תכסה בה', so 'וראיתם אותו' excludes a night garment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A night garment is exempt from ציצית, so ציצית is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא and רבי שמעון exempts women.

steps.title: Why include the blind person's garment and not the night garment?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own choice. Why should one פסוק include a blind person's garment while the other excludes a night garment, and not the reverse?
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to include the garment of a blind person and to exclude a nighttime garment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why it matched the two פסוקים this particular way. It could have included the night garment and excluded the blind person's garment instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have one פסוק that includes and one פסוק that excludes. Both the blind person's garment and the night garment share the same problem: the wearer cannot see the ציצית. So the ברייתא wants a reason for which garment goes into which group.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? This is a way of asking why you chose one option over the other
To include, meaning to bring a case into the law
To exclude, meaning to take a case out of the law

phrases.english: And what did you see
to include the garment of a blind person
phrases.notes: This inclusion comes from the other פסוק we just saw (step 28), 'אשר תכסה בה', דברים 22:12.

phrases.english: and to exclude a nighttime garment?
phrases.notes: This exclusion comes from 'וראיתם אותו', במדבר 15:39.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 28 split the two cases between the including פסוק and the excluding פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to include a blind person's garment and exclude a night garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both cases the wearer cannot see the ציצית, so the opposite split seems just as reasonable.

steps.title: Others can see a blind person's garment, but nobody sees at night
steps.stepSummary: A blind person's garment is still visible to other people, so it is included. A night garment is not visible to anyone, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the garment of a blind person, because other people can see it. I exclude a nighttime garment, because even other people cannot see it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. It points out a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וראיתם אותו' does not require that the wearer himself sees the ציצית. It is enough that the ציצית can be seen at all. In daytime others can see the blind man's ציצית, but at night no one can, so only the night garment falls outside 'seeing'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is in a state of being seen, meaning it can be seen
By others, meaning by people other than the wearer

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, what matters for ציצית is whether the garment can be seen by anyone, not only by the wearer. That is why a blind person is obligated but a night garment is exempt.

phrases.english: I include the garment of a blind person
which is visible to others,
and I exclude a nighttime garment
which is not visible to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי כְּסוּת סוֹמֵא שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָהּ בִּרְאִיָּה אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 by finding a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the blind man's garment and the night garment seem equal, since the wearer cannot see the ציצית in either case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeing by others counts. A blind man's garment is seen by others, while a night garment is seen by no one, so only the night garment is excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of רבי שמעון's source for exempting a night garment from ציצית.

steps.title: Turning to the view of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a question about the רבנן, who disagree with רבי שמעון. The question will be finished in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן...
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next question. The גמרא is about to ask how the רבנן, who do obligate a night garment, explain 'וראיתם אותו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון used 'וראיתם אותו' to exempt a night garment. The רבנן disagree, so the גמרא needs to know what they learn from this פסוק. The full question continues after this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, meaning the majority opinion that disagrees with רבי שמעון here

phrases.english: And the Rabbis

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי שמעון's source, the גמרא turns to the opposing view of the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן, who obligate a night garment, explain the words 'וראיתם אותו'
